business_summary.text: Pitti Engineering is an integrated manufacturer of electrical laminations, castings, and machine components for diverse industries.

call_points.text: Management reiterated FY27 lamination volume target of 82,000 tons.
Expansion backed by demand from Caterpillar, Voith, Progress Rail, Siemens Mobility and Medha Servo across data centres, mining, off-highway and railways.
Q2FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin at 15.8%, down from 16.8% a year ago.
call_points.versus_prior: FY27 guidance of margins similar to FY26 remains to be tested

call_points.text: Machining utilisation rose to 78% in Q2FY27 from 76% a year ago; castings utilisation fell to 77% from 90%.
FY27 revenue targeted at ₹2,300 Cr from 78,000 t laminations and 16,000 t machine components.
FY27 margins expected similar in percentage terms to FY26.
Machine hour capacity to rise from 7,20,000 to 10.8 lakh hours, commissioned in phases from FY28.
Data centre business adds three clients; commercial revenue expected from Q3FY27.
Q4 gross margin hit by ₹20 Cr of unexecuted high-value sales and a spike in March energy costs.
Net debt at ₹570-odd Cr; ₹125 Cr working capital release to bring it to ₹470-odd Cr.
Tax rate to stay around 33% due to ESOP, hedge accounting and depreciation differences.
Q1FY27 will remain slow on exports; no sharp recovery expected.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Dakshin Foundry Private Limited (DFPL) is contesting an order dated 22nd November 2025 passed by the Joint Commissioner of Central Tax, Bengaluru, for FY 2018-19 to FY 2022-23 relating to ITC availed. The demand comprises tax of Rs.3.09 crores along with applicable interest and equivalent penalty thereon. DFPL is contesting an order dated 11th November 2025 passed by the Superintendent of Central Tax, Bengaluru, for FY 2018-19 to FY 2022-23 relating to ITC, interest, penalties and an alleged RCM short-payment. The demand comprises tax of Rs. 0.01 crore, along with applicable interest and equivalent penalty thereon. DFPL is contesting an order dated 31st October 2025 passed by Asst Commissioner of Central Tax, Bengaluru, for FY 2018-19 to FY 2022-23 relating ITC reversal, short payment of GST and wrong availing of GST. The demand comprises tax of Rs.1.81 crore, along with applicable interest and equivalent penalty thereon.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: First Appellate Authority. Commissioner of Central Tax (Appeals), Bengaluru
tax_litigation.status: Pursuant to the amalgamation of DFPL with the Company, which became effective on 23rd September 2026, the litigation, along with all associated rights, obligations and liabilities, have vested in the Company. Total Demand of Rs. 4.91 crore along with applicable interest and equivalent penalty thereon. Based on merits of the case and the Company’s assessment, the Company believes that the demand is not sustainable and expects a favourable outcome. The matter is not expected to have any material impact on the Company's financial position or operations. The demand has been disclosed as a contingent liability in the Company's Consolidated Financial Statements. The appeal is pending adjudication. Detailed submissions have been filed and the matter is awaiting further proceedings.

operating_notes.text: Consolidated Q4FY26 revenue split: India ₹367.47 Cr, outside India ₹133.62 Cr.
Scheme of amalgamation of Pitti Industries Private Limited and Dakshin Foundry Private Limited into Pitti Engineering has an appointed date of 1 April 2026, pending NCLT approval.
Approved ₹290 Cr capex for greenfield casting and machined components facility in Macharam, Telangana.
Announced ₹290 Cr greenfield capex for casting and machined components facility in Macharam, Telangana, targeted for Q1FY30.
Greenfield casting facility planned with ₹290 crore capex, targeting commissioning by Q1FY30 with expected asset turns of 1.0–1.2x.
FY26 capacity utilisation: sheet metal 76%, machining 81%, casting 71%; Q4FY26: 80%, 87%, 64% respectively.
FY26 volumes: lamination 69,500 t (+10% YoY), casting and machine components 12,012 t (+15.4% YoY).
Machine components mix: 80% export, 20% domestic; high value-added assemblies 33-40% export.
Consolidated machining capacity is 7,20,000 hours at ~81% utilisation, proposed to rise to 10,80,000 hours under the greenfield casting and machined components capex.
Q2FY27 capacity utilisation ~78% for sheet metal and ~85% for machining.
Existing capacity as on 30-Sep-2026: sheet metal 1,08,000 MT per annum and 8,13,600 machining hours; post-expansion 1,60,000 MT and 13,14,000 hours.
PIPL and DFPL amalgamated into the company effective 23 September 2026 with appointed date 1 April 2026; the company has no subsidiaries as at the reporting date.
Board approved ₹450 Cr capex to expand sheet metal capacity to 1,60,000 MT and machine hours to 13,14,000 by FY31.
Q2FY27 high-value lamination assembly volumes rose 51.1% YoY to 4,786 MT.
Q2FY27 castings utilisation fell to 77% from 90% a year ago.
Phased investments of ~₹740 Cr to lift sheet metal capacity to 1,60,000 MT, castings to 36,000 MT and machining to 13,14,000 hours by FY31.
Board approved ₹450 Cr capex to expand sheet metal capacity to 160,000 MT by FY31.

timeline.summary: Pitti Engineering received credit rating assignments and affirmations of IND AA-/Stable/IND A1+ from India Ratings for ₹1,542 Cr of bank loan facilities.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹501.09 Cr (+6.9% YoY), net profit ₹26.61 Cr.
Pitti Engineering’s Board, chaired by **Mary Monica Braganza**, recommended ₹2.50 (50%) final dividend per ₹5 equity share for FY2026, pending AGM approval on May 14, 2026.
On May 14, 2026, Pitti Engineering approved a ₹290 Cr capex for a greenfield casting and machined components facility in Telangana.
Pitti Engineering reported FY26 consolidated total income of ₹1,953 Cr and announced a ₹290 Cr greenfield capex to double casting capacity by Q1FY30.
Pitti Engineering rescheduled its Investor Earnings Call from May 15 to May 18, 2026, at 1:00 PM IST to discuss Q4 & FY26 performance with MD & CEO Akshay S. Pitti.
Pitti Engineering announced a ₹290 crore greenfield capex to expand casting capacity to 36,000 MT by Q1FY30.
Pitti Engineering's Q4 & FY26 earnings call on 18 May 2026 guided FY27 revenue to ₹2,300 Cr and detailed a ₹290 Cr greenfield casting capex for Q1FY30 commissioning.

Pitti Engineering issued an addendum on 3 June 2026 to its 14 May 2026 capex notice, adding the machining capacity details: 7,20,000 hours existing at ~81% utilisation, to be raised to 10,80,000 hours.
Pitti Engineering concluded its Maharashtra GST search proceedings, agreeing to discharge ₹0.63 Cr tax and ₹0.15 Cr interest.
Q2FY27 results (standalone): revenue ₹578.44 Cr, net profit ₹33.89 Cr (-4.7% YoY).

Pitti Engineering Limited’s Board, chaired by **Mary Monica Braganza**, declared ₹2.00 (40%) interim dividend per ₹5 equity share on October 22, 2026, payable by November 21, 2026, with record date November 2.
Pitti Engineering's board approved a ₹450 Cr capex to expand sheet metal and machining capacities up to FY31.
Pitti Engineering's Q2FY27 investor presentation showed revenue up 21.1% YoY to ₹578.4 Cr but adjusted PAT down 15.1% to ₹36.3 Cr, with a ~₹740 Cr phased capacity expansion to FY31.
Pitti Engineering reported Q2FY27 revenue of ₹581 Cr and announced a ₹450 Cr capex to expand lamination and machining capacity by FY31.
